Explore my CV

The starting point

Automation can repeat requests, receive incomplete data or act on state that has already changed. This personal case explores making those situations explicit before connecting an interface, API and approval workflow.

How I built it

  • A contract with a business identifier, category, priority and idempotency key. Invalid input creates no records.
  • A C# domain separated from the ASP.NET Core 10 API. Bounded process memory, concurrency locking and states with an expected version.
  • Recognised replay with the same data; 409 for keys reused with different content, duplicate identifiers or old versions.
  • Review and approval as explicit transitions. Each change retains an event and does not allow skipping from the beginning to completed.
  • A local JavaScript demo and .NET domain verified with the same 18 scenario steps, plus concurrency and actual HTTP checks.
  • A Power Automate guide for retaining identifiers, waiting for approval and separating error recovery from retries.

The result

An ES/EN lab for observing both the successful path and conflicts. The repository includes the runnable API, OpenAPI contract, scenarios and checks. This is newly authored demonstration work, with no claimed commercial outcomes.

Run .NET and reproduce the checksRetries and approvals: technical note

Example boundaries

  • The website reproduces the logic in this tab; it does not call a server or submit real requests.
  • The API runs locally with process memory. Restarting loses records. It includes no identity, roles, database or exactly-once execution guarantee.
  • The Power Automate document is a guide, not a flow deployed in a tenant; no connectors have been purchased. Deployment requires the environment’s permissions, connectivity and licences.

What we store

The at_consent cookie remembers your choice for six months. Optional settings are stored locally for the same period. You can withdraw permission here: those settings will be deleted. Controls still work during your visit if you choose necessary only. If you enable the demo’s optional AI, the browser may store model files; delete them from the demo itself.
